cluster_name: Hague tribunal convicts Kosovo ex-president Thaci for war crimes
tldr: Headlines across the corpus converge on a single hard fact — conviction plus a 25-year sentence — producing a narrower, more uniform register than the body text. The Kosovo-Serbia political split surfaces in Balkan and German titles, while Russia's RT uniquely relabels Thaci a 'NATO-backed separatist' rather than a president, the starkest ideological divergence visible at the homepage layer.
event_summary: On September 16, 2026, the Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague convicted former President Hashim Thaci of war crimes and sentenced him to 25 years in prison; three other former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders were also convicted on charges arising from the 1998–99 Kosovo war.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet to strip Thaci's presidential title and substitute 'NATO-backed Kosovo separatist' — reorienting the verdict as a critique of Western Balkans policy rather than an international justice milestone, a framing absent from every other headline in the corpus.

The only headline to pack both Kosovo's rejection ('Unjust') and the Serbian minister's endorsement ('Applauds') into a single title, making the bilateral political split visible at a glance — no other outlet manages this contrast at headline level.

The only explainer-format headline in the corpus ('Why... Explained'), treating the conviction's legal basis as non-obvious and requiring justification — a different narrative posture than all other outlets, which present the verdict as a self-evident news event.

bottom_line: The headline layer condenses the Thaci verdict into a straightforward crime-and-punishment event for most global outlets, with only Balkan and German titles surfacing the Kosovo-Serbia political divide and Russia's RT uniquely reframing the defendant as a 'NATO-backed separatist' rather than a former head of state.
